evals.name: tokens-only-branded-surface
evals.prompt: We're building a tiny static marketing page with plain HTML and a single CSS file (no framework, no JS components). I want it to look like Grantcodes: brand background and text, rounded pricing callout, brand font. How should I wire up the styles?
evals.expected_output: A tokens-only setup using @grantcodes/style-dictionary/grantcodes/css plus the Greycliff font entrypoint, semantic --g-* tokens in consumer CSS (background/content/border, spacing, radius, typography), and no @grantcodes/ui or @grantcodes/astro dependency.
assertions: Imports @grantcodes/style-dictionary/grantcodes/css (and optionally the greycliff font entrypoint)
Does not introduce @grantcodes/ui, @grantcodes/astro, or React/Astro setup
Does not use obsolete --g-theme-* names or reference-tier --g-ref-* tokens in the consumer CSS
Does not claim automatic theme injection outside Astro

evals.name: react-settings-panel
evals.prompt: In our React 19 app I need a settings panel: email field with help text, a couple of grouped notification checkboxes, an options popover with extra filters, a success message after save, and a confirmation dialog before resetting. We already use @grantcodes/ui/react. Show the component structure and how to hook up the interactions.
evals.expected_output: FormField wrapping native email/checkbox controls, Popover with onToggle, Notice or Toast with onDismiss, Dialog opened via open state, only real wrapper exports, real boolean props, and accessible names/labels.
assertions: Imports FormField, Popover, Dialog, and a feedback component from @grantcodes/ui/react without inventing exports
Uses native input/checkbox controls with name, label/help, and no invented Switch/Checkbox component
Uses React boolean props (not string "false") for default-true properties such as Dialog dismissible or Toast dismissible
Uses Popover onToggle and/or Toast onDismiss correctly, without inventing Dialog close or Notice dismiss callbacks
Shows a dialog open state and/or trigger wiring rather than claiming a show()/hide() method
Maintains accessible control names and does not rely on colour-only feedback

evals.name: astro-landing-page
evals.prompt: Build the landing page for our new community workshop in Astro 7. I want a hero, three feature cards, pricing, two testimonials, a newsletter signup, and an FAQ accordion. The FAQ answers come from our CMS as HTML. We already have @grantcodes/astro installed.
evals.expected_output: ui({ theme: 'grantcodes' }) in astro.config with manual base.css import, blocks from @grantcodes/astro/blocks with correct props (Cards uses cards, Accordion items with trusted htmlContent), and a justified hydration decision.
assertions: Configures ui() with an explicit theme (and keeps base.css import manual) rather than claiming base/theme CSS is automatic
Imports the required blocks from @grantcodes/astro/blocks and uses Cards cards= (not items=)
Uses Accordion items with htmlContent for CMS HTML and flags/sanitizes it as trusted content
Uses Newsletter with a real action endpoint and Pricing with cta/included fields
Justifies hydration (or lack of it) rather than adding client:* directives to every block
Does not use the retired @grantcodes/astro-blocks package
